findings.title: The rebuild remedy for an installed nightly b<N> build now builds a different build, which can mean forcing a rebuild of a release that is already installed
findings.cause: rebuild_remedy still prints `ai-ctl build <project> --ref <id> --force` for every current build. Builder::build now names a build after the newest vX.Y.Z tag at the checked-out commit, or after the short commit when no release tags it. A legacy id such as b12359 or b12227 is neither, so the remedy cannot rebuild it under its own name.
findings.consequence: Suppose the current llama.cpp build is one of the nightly builds this machine still holds (b12111, b12227 or b12359, made current again with `build use`), and its build.json can no longer be read or its smoke test fails. doctor and `gateway config` then tell the user to run `ai-ctl build llama.cpp --ref b12359 --force`. That command checks out b12359 and builds it as v1.0.0. If v1.0.0 is already installed, --force rebuilds that healthy build, then makes v1.0.0 current. For b12227 it builds a new id named after the short commit. In both cases the broken nightly directory stays where it was, though the remedy reads as rebuilding that build in place.
findings.fix: In rebuild_remedy, give `ai-ctl build <project>` (the newest release) for an id that the recipe's tags do not read as a release and that is not a short commit: that is, a legacy nightly id.
findings.test: doctor's builds_check, with a current b12359 that cannot be read, gives the remedy `ai-ctl build llama.cpp`, not `--ref b12359 --force`. It fails before the fix.
findings.evidence: read: src/application/build.rs:136-143: the id is `recipe.tags.newest(checkout.tags)`, otherwise `BuildId::from_commit`. The test a_commit_both_forms_tag_is_built_under_its_version shows `--ref b12359` building v1.0.0. reproduced: `ls ~/.local/share/ai-ctl/builds/llama.cpp` lists b12111, b12227, b12359 and v1.0.0, so these legacy nightly ids are installed on this machine.
findings.fingerprint: bugs | docs/security.md + src/application/build.rs + src/application/doctor.rs | Builder::build + Current::installed + builds_check + rebuild_remedy + top level

findings.title: no test checks out an annotated release tag, which every llama.cpp release now is
findings.cause: the scope reworked the Upstream repository to stand for llama.cpp's vX.Y.Z releases, but its releases v0.1.0, v0.2.0 and v0.10.0 stay lightweight tags; only v0.10.0-rc is annotated, and no test checks it out. llama.cpp's v1.0.0 is an annotated tag (git cat-file -t v1.0.0 in its clone: tag; the capture llama.cpp-git-ls-remote.txt lists each release's tag object), as are whisper.cpp's v1.9.5 and audio.cpp's v0.9.4, while its nightly b12359 is lightweight. So nothing checks that rev_parse peels the tag object down to its commit
findings.consequence: rev_parse's revision changed from `{revision}^{commit}` to `{revision}^{object}` passes every test (908 passed). With that change, checking out llama.cpp v1.0.0 resolves to the tag object's hash. build.json, build list and each benchmark run then record that hash as the build's commit, and `git tag --points-at` on it leaves out b12359 and v1.0.0-b12359-b1b770d. The build is still named v1.0.0, so nothing fails and nothing flags the wrong commit
findings.fix: add a test to src/infrastructure/git.rs that tags the Upstream's third commit with an annotated v0.11.0 and a lightweight b12359, checks out v0.11.0, and asserts the checkout's commit is that commit and its tags are b12359, v0.10.0, v0.10.0-rc and v0.11.0. Or make the Upstream's release tags annotated, as llama.cpp's are
findings.test: an_annotated_release_is_checked_out_at_its_commit_under_each_of_its_tags; it passes on the code (1 passed) and fails under `^{object}` (left: the tag object's hash, right: the commit). Under `^{object}` it is the only test of the whole suite that fails. It runs git in a scratch repository and depends on no timing
findings.evidence: reproduced: in a copy at 0ce63e3, cargo test --lib an_annotated_release: ok. With `let peeled = format!("{revision}^{{object}}")`, cargo test: 908 passed, 1 failed, the new test only. Dropping the peel entirely is instead caught by an_unknown_reference_is_refused, since a 40-zero hash then verifies. read: git -C ~/.local/share/ai-ctl/sources/llama.cpp cat-file -t v1.0.0 prints tag, and -t b12359 prints commit
findings.fingerprint: tests | src/domain/recipe.rs + src/infrastructure/git.rs | GitSources::checkout + LLAMA_CPP + rev_parse + tests::upstream

findings.title: releases_of defaults a missing prerelease to False only so the older trimmed captures still parse
findings.cause: GitHub's release object always carries prerelease, as the new capture github-releases-ggml-org-llama.cpp-v1.0.0.http shows; the three older captures (llama-swap, llama.cpp b12242, stable-diffusion.cpp) were trimmed to tag_name, created_at and body, and item.get("prerelease", False) is the shim that keeps them parsing, with no LEGACY comment naming that obligation
findings.consequence: an answer from GitHub that lacks prerelease, a shape the script was not written for, is read as a page of releases instead of refused as "no release list", as a missing tag_name, created_at or body is; a nightly page would then come back as releases again with nothing said, and the next reader cannot tell the default from a rule of GitHub's API
findings.fix: read item["prerelease"] like the other three fields, so a missing field takes the KeyError path to DependencyError, and capture the three older pages again with prerelease among the kept fields (listed again in tests/fixtures/README.md); or, if recapturing costs more than the shim, keep the default under a comment `# LEGACY:` naming the captures made before 2026-11-14 without prerelease as its obligation
findings.test: in test_dependencies.py, the refused bodies of the "no release list" test gain one without prerelease, '[{"tag_name": "v271", "created_at": "2026-11-08T05:16:44Z", "body": ""}]', which fails today because the default reads it as a release
findings.evidence: read: dependencies.py:382-385 at 0ce63e3, the only field with a default; grep -c prerelease on tests/fixtures/github-releases-*.http gives 0 for the llama-swap, llama.cpp and stable-diffusion.cpp captures and 1 for llama.cpp-v1.0.0; tests/fixtures/README.md:288-291 says the older captures keep only tag_name, created_at and body; test_dependencies.py:491-526 builds its own pages without prerelease too
